2023_078_hs_cdb_23_24.paragraph: The 2023-2024 Course Descriptions book for Athens High School and Troy High School, revised January 2023 and issued under Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent of Schools, catalogs the credit-bearing courses offered at Troy School District's two comprehensive high schools together with graduation requirements, the district nondiscrimination policy, and the Oakland Schools Technical Campus option. Graduation requires 22.5 total credits, of which 18.50 are specified required credits spanning English, mathematics, science, social studies, physical education, health, world language/fine and applied arts/CTE, plus a non-credit 20-hour online learning experience.
2023_078_hs_cdb_23_24.page:
Publication
Course Descriptions for Athens High School and Troy High School, 2023-2024, Troy School District; revised January 2023; Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent of Schools. Athens High School: Dr. Lara Dixon, Principal, 4333 John R. Road, Troy, Michigan 48085 (main 248.823.2900, counseling 248.823.2962). Troy High School: Mr. Remo Roncone, Principal, 4777 Northfield Parkway, Troy, Michigan 48098 (main 248.823.2700, counseling 248.823.2715). Back matter lists the Department of Teaching & Learning, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.5221.

Nondiscrimination
The statement cites Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and the Americans with Disabilities Act. Jordan M. Harris, J.D., Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, is the Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator for employment and personnel matters, at 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098-4799, (248) 823-4000. The Director of Special Education is the Section 504/ADA Coordinator for handicapped and suspected handicapped students.

Graduation requirements (Class of 2023 and beyond)

| Department | Required credits |
| --- | --- |
| English | 4.0 |
| Science | 3.0 |
| Mathematics | 4.0 |
| Social Studies | 3.0 |
| Physical Education | 1.0 |
| Health | 0.5 |
| World Language, Fine & Applied Arts, CTE | 3.0 |
| Online Learning | 0.0 |
| State Assessments | 0.0 |
| Total Required Credits | 18.50 |
| Total Credits Needed for Graduation | 22.5 |

English 9 becomes a 1.0 credit requirement beginning with the class of 2027. Science for the class of 2027 is Biology 1.0, Chemistry 0.5/Physics 0.5, and Earth Science 0.5/Science Elective 0.5; for the classes of '24, '25 and '26 it remains Biology 1.0, Chemistry or Physics 1.0, and a Science Elective 1.0. Mathematics is Algebra 1, Geometry, Algebra 2 (or Algebra 2 Part A and Part B, or CTE program completion such as OSTC) and a math elective; four math credits must be earned while enrolled in high school and at least 1.0 credit of math or a math-related course in the final year. Physical Education is Intro to Physical Activity 0.5 plus a P.E. elective 0.5. A 1.0 credit VPAA requirement covers Industrial Technology, Business and Life Skills classes. The world language block is met by 2.0 credits of world language (non-sequential accepted) or 1.0 credit plus 1.0 credit of CTE or VPAA. State assessment requirements may be waived for the classes of 2021 and 2022.

Flexibility options (Class of 2016 and beyond, updated 9.2015, MCL 380.1278a and MCL 380.1278b)
Personal Curriculum aligned to a student's Educational Development Plan; excusal from the 0.5 P.E. elective for two seasons of district athletics or marching band, tracked automatically with no forms; world language flexibility for heritage or international proficiency; and CTE program completion exchanged 1:1 for required science, world language, or Algebra 2 credit.

Course catalog
Departments covered are Business, Career Technical Education, Industrial Technical, Life Skills, English, English Language Development, Fine Arts (Visual Arts, Music, Theatre Arts), Health, Mathematics, Media, Multi-Departmental, Physical Education, Science, Social Studies, Special Education, and World Language (French, Spanish, Japanese, Chinese, German). Each entry gives a course number, grade levels, length and credit, retake rules, and prerequisites; where no school is named the course runs at both high schools.

Oakland Schools Technical Campus
OSTC-Southeast at 5055 Delemere Street, north of 14 Mile between Crooks and Coolidge, serves grades 11-12 in two sessions, 08101 Session 1 AM and 08102 Session 2 PM, generally 1.5 credits per semester. OSTC credits are not NCAA approved; applications are made at www.ostconline.com by the end of February.

Grievance procedure
The antidiscrimination procedure runs three steps through the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services and then the Superintendent, whose written answer is final and binding.

Publication and contacts. The 2023-2024 Course Descriptions book covers Athens High School and Troy High School in the Troy School District, was revised January 2023, and carries the name of Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent of Schools. Athens High School is led by Principal Dr. Lara Dixon at 4333 John R. Road, Troy, Michigan 48085 (main office 248.823.2900, fax 248.823.2913, counseling 248.823.2962, attendance 248.823.2901). Troy High School is led by Principal Mr. Remo Roncone at 4777 Northfield Parkway, Troy, Michigan 48098 (main office 248.823.2700, fax 248.823.2713, counseling 248.823.2715, attendance 248.823.2701). The closing page lists the Department of Teaching & Learning at 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.5221; the Special Education section directs inquiries to Central Office Special Education at 248.823.5096.

Nondiscrimination. The opening statement cites Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and the Americans with Disabilities Act. Jordan M. Harris, J.D., Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, is the appointed Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator for employment and personnel matters, at Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098-4799, (248) 823-4000; the Director of Special Education is Section 504/ADA Coordinator for handicapped and suspected handicapped students. Bargaining-unit employees may alternatively use the grievance procedure in their collective bargaining agreement.

Graduation requirements, Class of 2023 and beyond. English requires 4.0 credits: English 9 for 1.0 credit beginning with the class of 2027, English 10 Lit/Comp 1 & 2, English 11 Lit/Comp plus an English elective or 11 English AP 1 & 2, and English 12 Lit/Comp 1 & 2 or 12 English AP 1 & 2, each 1.0 credit. Science requires 3.0 credits; class of 2027 requirements are Biology 1.0 credit, Chemistry 0.5 credit/Physics 0.5 credit, and Earth Science 0.5 credit/Science Elective 0.5 credit, while the current requirements for the classes of '24, '25 and '26 are Biology 1.0, Chemistry or Physics 1.0, and Science Elective 1.0. Mathematics requires 4.0 credits: Algebra 1, Geometry, Algebra 2 or Algebra 2 Part A and Part B (or CTE program completion such as OSTC), and a math elective, each 1.0 credit; high school math credits may be earned through a Troy middle school, but four credits must be earned while enrolled in high school and at least 1.0 credit of math or a math-related course must be completed in the final year. Social Studies requires 3.0 credits: World History/Geography 1 & 2 for 1.0, American History/Geography 1 & 2 for 1.0, Economics 0.5, and Government and Civics 0.5. Physical Education requires 1.0 credit (Intro to Physical Activity 0.5 plus a P.E. elective 0.5) and Health 0.5 credit. A 1.0 credit VPAA requirement covers Industrial Technology, Business and Life Skills classes. The World Language, Fine & Applied Arts, CTE block requires 3.0 credits, met by 2.0 credits of world language (non-sequential accepted) or 1.0 credit of world language plus 1.0 credit of CTE or VPAA. Online Learning carries 0.0 credit but requires a 20-hour on-line experience embedded across middle and high school. State Assessments carry 0.0 credit; requirements may be waived for the classes of 2021 and 2022. Total required credits are 18.50 and total credits needed for graduation are 22.5. Credit-bearing high school courses taken before matriculation appear on the Troy transcript with grades earned, and a retaken course grade replaces the initial grade unless prior administrative approval is granted.

Flexibility options, Class of 2016 and beyond, updated 9.2015, citing MCL 380.1278a and MCL 380.1278b. A Personal Curriculum permits substituted core credits aligned to the Educational Development Plan. Two seasons of Troy School District athletics or two seasons of marching band excuse the 0.5 credit P.E. elective, tracked automatically with no forms required. World language flexibility exists for non-English heritage proficiency, international study and residence, and CTE or Visual & Performing or Applied Arts substitution, documented by Personal Curriculum. CTE program completion exchanges credits 1:1 for required science or world language, or satisfies Algebra 2 where that content is embedded.

Business. Accounting 1 (005002), Accounting 2 (005022) and Financial Management (005122) each satisfy one-half credit of the math-related graduation requirement in the 12th grade year. Business & Personal Law 1 (005052) and Business & Personal Law 2 (005062, Troy High) may be taken in any order. Also offered are Business Management and Technology (005242) and Business Entrepreneurship (005232). Junior Business Internship Co-op (105024/205024) requires 10 or more accumulated credits and Senior Business Internship Co-op (108844/208844) requires 14.5 or more, awarding up to 2.0 credits for work of at least 10 hours per week and 200 hours per semester. Web Creation 1 (005272) and Web Page Creation 2 (005282) use the CS3 suite. Marketing includes Marketing 1 (005222), Marketing 2: Sales & Social Media Marketing (005252), Honors Marketing (005223, preparing for the Principles of Marketing CLEP examination), Sports and Entertainment Marketing (005182) with a Troy Athens Fantasy League, School-Based Enterprise (005113) for 12th grade only, and Marketing Internship Co-Op (005214) with 2 credit potential.

Career Technical Education. Careers in Education 1 (007393, Athens) and 2 (007403, Athens) use the Troy Athens Preschool; advanced placement credits are offered at Central University, Western Michigan University, Oakland University, Macomb Community College and Davenport University, with a Paraprofessional Certificate and, on completing both courses, a Child Development Associate (CDA) credential. Food service courses run the renovated Terrace Café restaurant lab on the ProStart curriculum with the ServSafe Sanitation Certificate available: Restaurant Operations/Terrace Cafe (007384, Athens, 2 hours, 2 credits), Commercial Baking (007373, Athens) and Commercial Foods (007473, Athens). Troy High automotive courses are 007003, 007294 (a 2-hour block requiring a C or better in Automotive Technology 1), 007213 and 007413, meeting NATEF Automotive Maintenance and Light Repair standards. Woodworking Design & Fabrication 1, 2 and 3 are 007163, 007173 and 007183; Mechatronics 1 A & B (108713/208713) and 2 A & B (108723/208723) cover CAD, CAM, CNC and 3D printing. Industrial Technical adds Architectural Drawing 1 and 2 (007072, 007082), Game Design 1 and 2 (007122, 007102, Athens) taught primarily in Java, and Introduction to Animation (007142) using 3DsMax.

Life Skills and Media. Parenthood/Child Development 1 and 2 (007242, 007262) are eligible for advanced placement credit at Oakland Community College. Other offerings are Essential Skills for Adulthood (009862), Personal Money Management (007272), Foods and Culture (007292, Troy High), Foods 2 (007282, Troy High), Fashion Design 1 and 2 (007332, 007342, Troy High), Stitchery (007372, Troy High) and Interior Design (007283, Troy High) using AutoCAD. Media includes Media Center Services (008492), Media Center Techniques (008502), and Innovation Learning/Innovation Lab (008682, 008692), influenced by the D school at Stanford University with references to creatinginnovators.com and dschool.stanford.edu.

English and English Language Development. Sequence numbers include 100063/200063 for 10 English Literature/Composition 1 and 2, 100073/200073 for the honors sections, 000082 for 11 English Literature/Composition, 100443/200443 for 11 English AP, 000113 for 12 English Lit/Comp and 000453 for 12 English AP 1 & 2. Electives include Creative Writing 1 and 2 (000182, 000192), Classical Mythology and Drama (000232), Film and Literature (000212), Literature of Suspense (000312), Science Fiction (000382), Voices in Literature (000132), Sports Literature (000322), Personal Communication (000352), Speech 1 and 2 (000392, 000142), Debate 1 and 2 (000492, 000502), Modern Shakespeare (000242), Writing for Publication in Journalism, Newspaper and Yearbook (100273/200273, 000333, 000343), Writing for Broadcasting (000342), Advanced Writing for Broadcasting (000362) and Advanced Publication Production (000353). Seminar AP and Research AP (002523, 002533) culminate in a paper of approximately 4000-5000 words with an oral defense. ELD placement uses the State of Michigan Entrance Protocol with annual WIDA Access administration; courses are Beginner ELD (101013/20103), Intermediate ELD (101023/201023), Advanced ELD (101033/201033), Bridges to Lit/Comp for ELs (101113/201113) and EL Tutorial (101103/201103), supported by rotating language support content classes including LS Biology (104703/204703), LS Introductory Physics (004313), LS World History/Geography (002272, 002282), LS American History/Geography (102703, 202703), LS Government/Civics (002092), LS Economics (002422) and LS Health (008862).

Fine Arts, Health and Physical Education. Visual arts span Multi-Media Art (006212), Mindful Art, Drawing and Advanced Drawing (006232, 006243), Painting (006252, 006263), Cartoons, Comics & Animation (006352), Ceramics (006272, 006283), Lettering & Calligraphy (006362), Studio Art (006373), Advanced Art AP (006393), Applied Arts and Design (006222), Computer Graphics (006422, 006433), Sculpture (006292) and photography (007112, 007114). Music includes Campus, Concert, Cadet and Symphonic Bands (006023, 006013, 006143, 006003), Jazz Ensemble and Jazz Explorations (006033, 006042), Color Guard (006002), Percussion (006104), Freshman, Concert, Symphony and Philharmonic Orchestras (006083, 006073, 006063, 006093), Treble and Concert Choir (006113, 006103), Mixed Chorus and Madrigal Singers (006123, 006133, Athens), Chorus/Choir Accompanist (006132), AP Music Theory (006053) and Intro to Music Technology and Recording (006501) using ProTools. Theatre I-III (000402, 000412, 000422) and Youth Theatre (000162) complete fine arts. Health (008852) is required for graduation; Peer Mediation (008573) is a grade 12 course. Physical education includes Intro to Physical Activity Level 1 and Level 2 (007952, 007962), Exercise and Lifelong Fitness (006162), Self Defense (006172), Net Sports & Fitness (008082), Fall and Spring Team Sports & Fitness (007972, 007992), Weight Training and Aerobics (007922, 007912), Tumbling & Gymnastics/Fitness (008042), Learning to Swim (007942), Lifeguarding/Advanced Swimming (008072, requiring students to be 15 years old with a $40 cost for Red Cross certification) and Strength and Conditioning (008014). The President's Challenge Physical Fitness Test is given in most classes.

Mathematics, Science and Social Studies. Math runs Algebra 1 (003043), Intensified Algebra 1 (103123/203123), Geometry (003063), Geometry Honors (003930), Algebra 2 Part A and B (003263, 003273), Algebra 2 (003093), Algebra 2 Honors (003183), Precalculus (003233), Precalculus Honors (003253), College Algebra (003023, Troy High), Calculus AB AP (003173), Calculus BC AP (003203), Statistics AP (003213), and dual-enrollment Calculus 3 (003212) and Linear Algebra (003222) through Lawrence Tech. Computing includes Computer Science 1 (003142, Troy High), AP Computer Science A (003162 at Troy High, 003163 at Athens), Computer Science Principles AP (003373), Cybersecurity (003172 THS, 103172/203172 AHS) and Introduction to Data Science (103383/203383), built on Python and citing Google, NASA and Netflix. Science includes Introductory Biology (004003), Biology: Anatomy and Physiology (004053), Genetics, Bacteriology, Biotechnology, and Embryology (004063), AP Biology (004073), Chemistry 1 and 2, Chemistry 2 AP (004243), Organic Chemistry (004102), Introductory Physics (004213), Physics 1 and 2 (004223, 004233), Physics 2 AP (004253), Physics C AP (004263), Astronomy (004212), Forensic Science (004042), Environmental Science (004222) and Environmental Science AP (004273). Social studies spans World History/Geography 1 and 2 (002232, 002242), Human Geography AP (002503), American History/Geography 1 and 2 (102023, 202023) covering the United States from 1877, American History/Geography AP (002013), Economics (002062), Economics AP (002073), Government and Civics (002072), Government AP (002052), World History/Geography AP (002233), Psychology 1 and 2 (002152, 002162), Psychology AP (002163), Sociology (002182), Mental Health (002112, Athens), Philosophy (002082, Athens), Comparative Government and Politics AP (002042) built around China, Great Britain, Iran, Mexico, Nigeria and Russia, Political Science (002322), Human Rights and The Law (002102), History of American Criminal Law (002032), History through Film (002034), Conflicts of the 20th & 21st Centuries (002502, Athens), Introduction to Leadership (002122), Leadership Lab (002125) and LINK (002222).

Special Education and World Language. Special education courses, placed with an IEP case manager and certified by an IEPT, include Achievement Skills 1A-4B (109909/209909, 109910/209910, 109911/209911, 109912/209912), Linguistics 2D, 2E and 2F (009273, 009283, 009263), Reading Strategies (009201), Integrated Math 1 and 2 (003003, 003103), English Language Arts 1 and 2 (009303, 009573), Math Skills A/B (009332/009342) and Life Skills Math (009632/009642). World language sequences are French 1-4 and French AP (000603, 000613, 000623, 000633, 000643), Spanish 1-4 and Spanish AP (000693, 000703, 000713, 000723, 000733), Japanese 1-4 and Japanese AP (000823, 000833, 000843, 000863, 008863), Chinese 1-4 and Chinese AP (000853, 000873, 000883, 000893, 000813), and German 1-4 (000653, 000663, 000673, 000683). Targets are stated against the ACTFL Proficiency Guidelines, from Novice-mid/Novice-high at level 1 to Intermediate-high/Advanced-low at AP. Japanese 2 students read and write 120 basic Kanji characters, Japanese 3 adds another 170 or more, and Japanese 4 adds another 180 or more.

Oakland Schools Technical Campus. OSTC-Southeast is at 5055 Delemere Street, north of 14 Mile between Crooks and Coolidge, on the Southeast Campus in Royal Oak, with a Northeast Campus in Pontiac. Programs serve grades 11-12 selectively; OSTC recommends high school credit per local district requirement, generally 1.5 credits per semester. If regular students carry six credits, OSTC students must carry three credits at their home high school plus three at OSTC. Sessions are 08101 Session 1 AM (classes begin 7:50 AM, dismissed 10:20 AM) and 08102 Session 2 PM (begin 12:00 PM, dismissed 2:30 PM). Programs include Automotive Technology and Cosmetology (each must begin in 11th grade), Collision Repair and Refinishing, Computer Programming, Computer Networking, Construction Technology, Culinary Arts/Hospitality, Electrical and Energy Technologies, Entrepreneurship & Advanced Marketing, Health Sciences, Machining, Mechatronics, Visual Imaging Technology, Welding, and Homeland Security (Criminal Justice or Cyber Security). A bus transports students to OSTC-SE, though afternoon-session students provide their own ride home. Applications are made at www.ostconline.com by the end of February, and athletes are warned that OSTC credits are not NCAA approved.

Grievance procedure. Written grievances alleging discrimination on the basis of sex including sexual harassment, race, color, religion, national origin, age (employees only), height, weight, marital status or handicap go to the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, the designated compliance administrator. Step 1 requires filing with the immediate supervisor within 10 workdays of the incident, a copy to the Assistant Superintendent not later than the next workday, a meeting within 5 workdays of filing, and a written answer within 3 workdays of the meeting. Step 2 allows appeal within 3 workdays, a meeting with the Assistant Superintendent or Deputy Superintendent within 10 workdays, and a written answer within 5 workdays. Step 3 allows appeal to the Superintendent within 3 workdays, a meeting within 10 workdays, and a written answer within 5 workdays that is final and binding. A grievance not filed or appealed within the time limits is deemed abandoned, failure to hold a meeting or render a decision allows automatic appeal to the next level, time limits may be extended only by mutual written agreement, and no record is kept in a staff member's personnel file if the final decision finds no reasonable basis.
